back: Stress: below about 1 700 m³ per person per year. Scarcity: below about 1 000 m³. Absolute scarcity: below about 500 m³.
About 97% of water is salt water; about 2.5-3% is fresh; about two thirds of fresh water is ice and almost 30% groundwater.
Capture, treatment and supply, use, disposal and reuse.
A lack of water resources to meet demand, as in arid regions or where withdrawals are too high.
Water exists but money, infrastructure or institutions to capture and deliver it are lacking.

front: Effects of deforestation on the water cycle
back: Less interception and transpiration; less infiltration; more runoff, erosion and flood risk.

front: Effects of urbanisation on the water cycle
back: More impermeable surfaces: more runoff, less infiltration and recharge, shorter lag times.
Agriculture (mostly irrigation) accounts for about 70% of global freshwater withdrawals.
A falling water table, reduced river flow, dry wells, saltwater intrusion near coasts and ground subsidence.
